summary:
Tokat province has no trans-specific statute, enforcement pattern or incident documentation of its own, and no region-specific signal was identified in the sources for this record.

The two sources that address Tokat do so only by placing the province inside Türkiye's nationwide regime of assembly bans. Any visible LGBT gathering in Tokat would be policed under the framework that has banned Pride in Istanbul and in other cities in most years since 2015, during which police have used tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against those who attempt to assemble.

Provincial authorities and police in Tokat therefore operate inside a documented national pattern in which visible LGBT assembly is routinely banned and policed. Human Rights Watch's World Report 2025, covering 2024, records Istanbul Pride banned for the tenth consecutive year and similar bans imposed by many cities across the country.
tangentialFactors:
All incident, detention and violation counts available to this record are national aggregates for Türkiye. No province-level breakdown is published, so Tokat's share of those totals cannot be derived from these sources, and a national raw count carries no information about conditions in Tokat specifically.

Tokat's exposure is derivative rather than local: changes to Türkiye's penal code and judicial packages apply province-wide without local variation, so what a visitor faces in Tokat tracks national legislative developments and the conduct of provincial police rather than any Tokat-specific rule.

No source compares provinces against one another or ranks them by incidents, so no relative positioning of Tokat among Türkiye's provinces is available.
localsOnly:
No Tokat-specific resident-facing provisions were identified. Rules governing legal gender recognition, discrimination protection, relationship recognition and custody for residents in Tokat are national in origin and are carried by the national record for Türkiye rather than restated here.

Residents of Tokat are subject to the same assembly-ban practice as elsewhere in the country, with provincial police applying national guidance on Pride and other visible LGBT gatherings; no Tokat-specific enforcement decision, permit refusal or prosecution is documented in the sources.
outOfScopeNotes:
Neither source that names Tokat documents an event observed in Tokat. Both use the province to illustrate a national pattern, so the application to Tokat is an extrapolation from country-wide practice rather than a locally reported finding.

No Tokat-specific incident, detention record, police conduct documentation, local detention facility data or hospital and care-access data was found in the sources. Whether any Pride or LGBT assembly has been attempted and banned in Tokat in a particular year is not sourced.

Whether the draft judicial package reported by Human Rights Watch on 29 October 2025 has since been enacted remains unresolved in the sources; the record also does not establish whether any later package's treatment of LGBTQ provisions would apply in Tokat differently from elsewhere.
